advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Thread `force_reclaim=True` through `run_git_write` (or expose it as a parameter) so the exclusively-locked txn/compact/delete/init paths force-reclaim a young orphan index.lock like event_append does.
evidence: src/rebar/_store/gitutil.py:257: `result = _with_index_lock_retry(str(tracker), lambda: _with_transient_head_retry(lambda: run_git(tracker, *args, check=False)),)` — no `force_reclaim` argument, defaults to False
src/rebar/_commands/txn.py:126: `cp = run_git_write(tracker_dir, *args, check=False)` inside `_git`, which runs the claim/transition add+commit
src/rebar/_commands/txn.py:177: `handle = _acquire_write_lock(tracker_dir)` — the transition path holds the exclusive write lock, the same invariant used to justify force-reclaim in event_append
Commit message asserts 'the four locked git helpers pass it,' omitting the equally-locked txn/compact/delete/init path that also runs under the write lock
advisory.finding: `run_git_write` (the txn.py transition/claim, compact, delete, and init write path) calls `_with_index_lock_retry` without `force_reclaim=True`, so a locked write on that path is still blocked behind the 300s stale threshold for a young orphan index.lock — the same Mode B cascade this change fixes for event_append. txn.py's `_git` holds the exclusive write lock (`_acquire_write_lock`) and mutates the index, so its orphan-under-lock invariant is identical, yet it was not updated.
scenarios: An OOM/SIGKILL leaves a young orphan index.lock, then a `rebar transition`/`claim` (txn.py) runs: it exhausts ~2s of retries and hard-fails, and every subsequent locked transition keeps failing until the 300s threshold elapses
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a `force_reclaim: bool = False` (or True for these locked callers) parameter to `run_git_write` and pass it into `_with_index_lock_retry`, then have txn.py's `_git` (and compact/delete/init, which run under the write lock) request it.
